As a developer, I want to analyze, documnet and give KT on the Web deep link framework. ---- *Notes* # Deep Link System — Knowledge Transfer## OverviewThe deep link system in `ahm-mep-ui-web` serves two distinct but related purposes:1. **Content Link Transformation** — parsing `$$internal:...$$` and `$$external:...$$` tokens embedded in CMS/API string content into navigable HTML anchor tags at render time.2. **URL-based Deep Linking** — enabling users (or external systems like email, push notifications, and SSO tokens) to land directly on a specific page/feature within the app, including handling the pre-auth state via cookie persistence.---## Architecture Map``` ┌──────────────────────────────┐ │ External trigger sources │ │ • Email / push notification │ │ • JWT token claims │ │ • In-app share links │ └──────────┬───────────────────┘ │ ┌─────────▼──────────┐ │ /dl?page=X │ (Next.js SSR page) │ /mobiledl │ └─────────┬──────────┘ │ ┌────────────────────▼────────────────────────┐ │ withDeepLink() HOC (getServerSideProps) │ │ • Reads JWT claims x-mah-deeplink │ │ • Detects dl/? in URL │ │ • If no session: stores via dpLinkSetUtil │ └────────────────────┬────────────────────────┘ │ ┌────────────────────▼────────────────────────┐ │ deepLinkHandlerUtil │ │ • dpLinkValidator() → resolved path │ │ • dpLinkSetUtil() → write cpValue │ │ • dpLinkGetUtil() → read cpValue │ │ • getUrl() → URL builder │ └────────────────────┬────────────────────────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────┐ │ customDeepLinkMapper (plugin handlers) │ │ • healthactionHandler (mehealthactioncategory) │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ Separately, within CMS/API string rendering: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ DeepLinkUtil (library/src/utils/DeepLinkUtil.ts) │ │ • identifyLinkType() → transforms $$...$$ tokens │ │ • internalDeepLinkObject() → returns {label, url} │ │ • externalDeepLinkHyperUrl() → adds target=""_blank"" │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘```---## Part 1 — Content Link Transformation (`DeepLinkUtil`)**Source:** `packages/library/src/utils/DeepLinkUtil.ts`### Token SyntaxCMS content and API responses embed navigation intents as plain-text tokens, never as raw HTML. `DeepLinkUtil` is the single place that transforms them.| Token format | Meaning ||---|---|| `$$internal:Label:path$$` | Link to an internal app route || `$$external:Label:https://...$$` | Link to an external URL (opens in new tab) |**Example tokens:**```$$internal:View Rewards:dl?page=phr&pageId=details&modal=reward$$$$external:Learn more:https://example.com/article$$$$external:Download PDF:{Content_URL}/files/guide.pdf$$```---### API Reference#### `identifyLinkType(str, aemAssetURL): string`The primary entry point used throughout the codebase. Runs both internal and external parsers sequentially on a raw HTML/text string.```tsimport DeepLinkShare from '@ahm-mep/library/DeepLinkUtil';const html = DeepLinkShare.identifyLinkType(apiResponseString, acsBaseUrl);// Returns a string with all $$...$$ tokens replaced by tags```Called from: Rewards, Notifications, Health Action, PHR, Coaching, Library atoms.---#### `internalDeepLinkHyperUrl(decodedStr): string`Replaces `$$internal:...$$` tokens with `` tags. The special path prefix `dl?` triggers enhanced logic:- `dl?page=X` (no modal) → `Label`- `dl?modal=X` (no page) → `Label` — the `{{DYNAMECONTEXT}}` placeholder is resolved by the rendering page at runtime.- Paths containing `sso-out-` → adds `target=""_blank""` to open SSO links in a new tab.- All other paths → `Label`**Regex:** `/\$\$internal:(.*?):(.*?)(?!&)(.*?)\$\$/g`---#### `internalDeepLinkObject(decodedStr): { label, url } | null`Returns a structured object instead of HTML. Used when the calling component needs the URL programmatically (navigation hooks, onClick handlers).```tsconst result = DeepLinkShare.internalDeepLinkObject('$$internal:Challenge:dl?page=challenge&pageId=details&challengeId=42$$');// { label: 'Challenge', url: '/dl?page=challenge&pageId=details&challengeId=42' }```Used by: `useChallengeDeepLink`, `AhmNotificationModal`, `Notification/index.tsx`.---#### `internalDeepLinkObjectForModal(decodedStr, isLandingPage): { label, url, isSameLandingPage } | undefined`Modal-aware variant. When `isLandingPage=true` and the URL contains a `modal` param, returns only the modal name as `url` so the current page can open it without navigation. When `isLandingPage=false`, strips empty `pageId` suffixes.---#### `externalDeepLinkHyperUrl(decodedStr, aemAssetURL): string`Replaces `$$external:Label:URL$$` with ``. Includes:- **`{Content_URL}` placeholder** — replaced with `aemAssetURL` before processing, enabling AEM-hosted assets.- **URL safety check** — only `https?:`, `mailto:`, `tel:` schemes are allowed; anything else becomes `href=""#""`.- **Accessibility** — if the link label is `""here""` or `""click here""` (non-descriptive), an `aria-label` is derived from the URL filename (e.g., `""Annual Report 2024 (PDF)""`).---#### `externalDeepLinkObject(decodedStr, aemAssetURL): { label, url } | null`Structured-object variant of the external parser. Returns `{ label, url }` or `null`.---#### `replaceURLforAEM(queryString, aemAssetURL): string`Replaces the `{Content_URL}` placeholder (case-insensitive) with the AEM base URL. Used internally by external link functions; exposed for direct use when a URL string alone needs transformation.---### Usage Pattern — Rendering CMS HTML```tsx// In a component that renders API-provided HTMLimport DeepLinkShare from '@ahm-mep/library/DeepLinkUtil';const processedHtml = DeepLinkShare.identifyLinkType(rawContent, config.acsBaseUrl);return
;```---## Part 2 — URL-Based Deep Link Navigation### Files| File | Role ||---|---|| `apps/host/src/components/utils/deepLinkHandlerUtil.tsx` | Core URL builder, validator, cookie utilities || `apps/host/src/components/utils/customDeepLinkMapper.ts` | Plugin handlers for module-specific URL logic || `apps/host/src/components/utils/withDeepLink.tsx` | SSR HOC — reads JWT claims, detects deep link in URL || `apps/host/src/pages/dl/index.tsx` | `/dl` route — entry point for URL-based deep links || `apps/host/src/pages/mobiledl/index.tsx` | `/mobiledl` route — native app redirect for mobile |---### Deep Link URL FormatAll web deep links arrive at `/dl` via a query string:```/dl/?page=&pageId=[&=][&modal=]```**Examples:**```/dl/?page=challenge&pageId=details&challengeId=101/dl/?page=challenge&pageId=teamdetails&challengeId=101&challengeConfigId=5/dl/?page=phr&pageId=details&modal=reward/dl/?page=hra/dl/?page=coaching&modal=program/dl/?page=mehealthactioncategory&pageId=42```---### Module-to-URL Mapping (`AHMMappingModule` enum)Defined in `apps/host/src/components/utils/deepLinkHandlerUtil.tsx`. Maps the `page=` query value to an app URL segment.| `page=` value | Resolves to ||---|---|| `explore` | `content` || `journey` | `my-journey?modal={modalName}` || `hra` | `health-risk-assessment` || `phr`, `healthaction`, `home`, `myprofile`, `healthchecklist`, `mehealthaction`, `mentalhealth` | `personal-health-record` (with optional modal) || `coaching` | `my-coaching/` || `challenge` | `challenge` || `tracker` | `tracker` || `mhs` | `my-health-score` || `myhealth100` | `personal-health-record/my-health/` || `heartcoins` | `personal-health-record/my-health/?modal=reward` || `rewards` | `personal-health-record/profile?modal=reward` || `deviceintegration` | `device-integration` || `phrcommunication` | `personal-health-record/communication` || `phrmessage` | `personal-health-record?modal=message` || `contactinformation` | `personal-health-record?modal=contactinformation` || `profilehealthchecklist` | `my-health-action?hcSelectedTab=1` || `myhealthchecklist` | `my-health-action` || `useremailupdate` | `user-update-contact` || `sso-out-{spid}` | `sso/?spid={spid}` (SSO pass-through) |---### `pageId` URL Templates (`urlMapper`)When both `page=` and `pageId=` are present, the `urlMapper` table provides a URL template. Placeholders like `{challengeId}` are filled from the remaining query params.| Key (`module_pageId`) | Template ||---|---|| `phr_heartcoins` | `my-health/?modal=reward` || `healthaction_education` | `/healthaction-checklist` || `challenge_details` | `{pageid}/{challengeId}` || `challenge_teamdetails` | `{pageid}/{challengeId}/{challengeConfigId}` || `challenge_myteam` | `{pageid}/{challengeId}/{challengeConfigId}` || `challenge_detail` | `?modal={modalName}` || `myhealth100_hadetails` | `?modal=healthactionchecklist` || `phr_details` | `?modal={modalName}` || `coaching_details` | `?modal={modalName}` || `journey_details` | `?modal={modalName}` || `journey` | `?modal={modalName}` || `explore_details` | `?modal={modalName}` || `hra_details` | `my-health` |---### `dpLinkValidator(deepLinkFullPath): string`**Source:** `apps/host/src/components/utils/deepLinkHandlerUtil.tsx`The main public validator. Takes a raw query string (the part after `/dl/?`) and returns a fully resolved app path.```tsdpLinkValidator('page=challenge&pageId=details&challengeId=101')// → 'challenge/details/101'dpLinkValidator('page=phr&modal=reward')// → 'personal-health-record?modal=reward'dpLinkValidator('page=hra')// → 'health-risk-assessment'dpLinkValidator('') // → '/'dpLinkValidator(undefined) // → '/'```**Internal flow:**```dpLinkValidator(path) → normalizePageIdParam() // normalises ""pageId"" → ""pageid"" → parseUrlParams() // splits ""key=value&..."" into an object → extractUrlComponents() // pulls out moduleName, pageId, modal → getUrl() // dispatches to the right builder ├─ isValidPageId? → handleUrlWithPageId() → customDeepLinkMapper check first ├─ isValidModal? → handleUrlWithModalOnly() └─ else → handleDefaultUrl() → trim trailing slash```---### `getUrl(moduleName, pageId, urlMapper, paramsObject, modal): string`Core URL assembly function. Decision logic:| Condition | Handler | Result ||---|---|---|| `pageId` is defined, non-empty, non-`""0""` | `handleUrlWithPageId` | Looks up `urlMapper[module_pageId]`, fills placeholders, prepends module base path || No `pageId`, but `modal` is present | `handleUrlWithModalOnly` | Uses `AHMMappingModule[module]`, replaces `{modalName}` || Neither `pageId` nor `modal` | `handleDefaultUrl` | Uses `AHMMappingModule[module]` as-is |---### Cookie-Based Deep Link PersistenceThe cookie `cpValue` (constant `DEEPLINKURL_STR`) stores a deep link for users who arrive at a protected page while unauthenticated.#### `dpLinkSetUtil(req, res)`Called server-side when there is no active session. Extracts the path after `dl/?` from the request URL and writes it into the `cpValue` cookie (TTL: `60 * 6 * 24` seconds = ~6 days).#### `dpLinkGetUtil(req, res): string | undefined`Called on the index page's `getServerSideProps` after auth completes. Reads and immediately deletes the `cpValue` cookie. Returns the stored path or `undefined`.**Important:** The cookie deletion is intentional (read-once semantics) — once consumed by the index page, `Checkpoint` either navigates immediately or re-stores the resolved path back into `cpValue` for `JourneyApp` to consume.---### `withDeepLink()` HOC**Source:** `apps/host/src/components/utils/withDeepLink.tsx`A `getServerSideProps` factory for the `/dl` page. It resolves the deep link path from two sources in priority order:1. **URL path** — if `dl/?` is present in `ctx.req.url`, extracts the query string and sets `dlActive=true`.2. **JWT ID token claims** — reads `x-mah-deeplink` (module name) and `x-mah-deeplink-id` (pageId) to build a `dl/?page=X&pageId=Y` path. Only triggers if both claims are non-empty and non-`""0""`.If no Auth0 session exists, calls `dpLinkSetUtil` to persist the deep link in a cookie before returning minimal props, allowing the login flow to redirect the user back after authentication.Props returned: `{ isMobile, deepLinkURL, dlActive, config, memberAccess, memberPlanId, supplierId, connection, memberRole }`.---### Custom Deep Link Handlers**Source:** `apps/host/src/components/utils/customDeepLinkMapper.ts`A plugin registry for modules that require non-standard URL construction. `handleUrlWithPageId` always checks this registry before applying the default `urlMapper` logic.**Current handler:**| Module | Condition | Output ||---|---|---|| `mehealthactioncategory` | `moduleName === 'mehealthactioncategory'` | `my-health-action/healthactioncategory/?sourcename=deeplink&meid={pageId}` |**Adding a new handler:**```ts// customDeepLinkMapper.tsconst myModuleHandler: CustomDeepLinkHandler = { condition: (params) => params.moduleName === 'mymodule', handler: (params) => `my-module-path/${params.pageId}`,};export const customDeepLinkHandlers: CustomDeepLinkHandler[] = [ healthactionHandler, myModuleHandler, // add here];```---## Part 3 — End-to-End Flows### Flow 1: Authenticated User Clicks a Deep Link URL```User visits /dl/?page=challenge&pageId=details&challengeId=101 ↓withDeepLink() SSR HOC → session exists → dlActive=true, deepLinkURL='page=challenge&...' ↓DeepLinkHandler component (dl/index.tsx) → dpLinkValidator('page=challenge&pageId=details&challengeId=101') → 'challenge/details/101' ↓router.push('challenge/details/101') → user lands on challenge detail page```---### Flow 2: Unauthenticated User Clicks a Deep Link URL```User visits /dl/?page=phr&modal=reward (no Auth0 session) ↓withDeepLink() SSR HOC → no session → dpLinkSetUtil() stores 'page=phr&modal=reward' in cpValue cookie → returns { dlActive: false } ↓User is redirected to login ↓After login, user lands on / (index.tsx getServerSideProps) → dpLinkGetUtil() reads & deletes cpValue → 'page=phr&modal=reward' → dpLinkValidator() → 'personal-health-record?modal=reward' → deepLink prop passed to ↓Checkpoint.redirectUser() → if email confirmed & tutorial done → router.push('personal-health-record?modal=reward') → else → setCookie('cpValue', resolvedPath) for JourneyApp to pick up ↓JourneyApp reads cpValue → if path does NOT start with 'page=' → router.push(path) + deleteCookie```---### Flow 3: Deep Link Embedded in CMS/API Content```API returns: ""Complete your $$internal:Health Assessment:dl?page=hra$$ today."" ↓Component calls DeepLinkShare.identifyLinkType(str, acsBaseUrl) ↓internalDeepLinkHyperUrl() matches $$internal:...$$ → page='hra', no modal, no pageId → returns: ""Complete your Health Assessment today."" ↓Rendered in
→ user clicks → navigates to /wellbeing/dl?page=hra → Flow 1 above```---### Flow 4: Challenge Share Link```useChallengeDeepLink({ challengeId: 101, competitionType: 'TEAM', challengeConfigId: 5 }) ↓generates: '$$internal:Challenge:dl?page=challenge&pageId=teamdetails&challengeId=101&challengeConfigId=5$$' ↓DeepLinkShare.internalDeepLinkObject(str) → { label: 'Challenge', url: '/dl?page=challenge&pageId=teamdetails&challengeId=101&challengeConfigId=5' } ↓setValue(window.location.origin + '/wellbeing' + url) → 'https://app.example.com/wellbeing/dl?page=challenge&...' → copied to clipboard or shared via native share sheet```---### Flow 5: JWT Token Deep Link (Email / External System)```SSO / identity provider includes in JWT ID token: x-mah-deeplink: 'coaching' x-mah-deeplink-id: '42' ↓withDeepLink() SSR HOC detects both claims → deepLinkPath = '/dl/?page=coaching&pageId=42' → dlActive = true ↓dl/index.tsx → dpLinkValidator('page=coaching&pageId=42') → handleUrlWithPageId('coaching', '42', urlMapper, {}, '') → urlMapper key 'coaching_42' not found → updatedURL = '' → reDirCode = 'my-coaching' → getValidURL('my-coaching', '42', '') → 'my-coaching/' ↓router.push('my-coaching/')```---### Flow 6: Mobile App Deep Link (`/mobiledl`)```User visits /mobiledl?... ↓withMobileDeepLink() detects iOS/Android via user-agent ↓iOS: window.location = '{mobileDLPackage}://' (custom URL scheme) setTimeout(2000) → fallback to App Store URL ↓Android: window.location = 'intent://{mobileDLAppname}#Intent;...' setTimeout(2000) → fallback to Play Store URL```Environment variables required: `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOBILE_DL_PACKAGE`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOBILE_DL_APPNAME`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOBILE_DL_APP_TITLE`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOBILE_DEEP_LINKING_ENABLED`.---## Part 4 — Adding Support for a New Module### Step 1 — Add to `AHMMappingModule`In `apps/host/src/components/utils/deepLinkHandlerUtil.tsx`:```tsexport enum AHMMappingModule { // ... existing entries mymodule = 'my-module-path',}```### Step 2 — Optionally add `pageId` templates to `urlMapper````tsconst urlMapper = { // ... existing entries mymodule_details: '{id}/detail',};```### Step 3 — Add a custom handler (if non-standard logic is needed)In `apps/host/src/components/utils/customDeepLinkMapper.ts`:```tsconst myModuleHandler: CustomDeepLinkHandler = { condition: (params) => params.moduleName === 'mymodule' && someCondition(params), handler: (params) => `my-module-path/${params.pageId}?extra=value`,};export const customDeepLinkHandlers = [healthactionHandler, myModuleHandler];```### Step 4 — Type declarationsAdd the module's type declaration to the relevant package's `@types/library/index.d.ts` if the package uses `@ahm-mep/library/DeepLinkUtil`.---## Part 5 — Key Files Summary| File | Purpose ||---|---|| `packages/library/src/utils/DeepLinkUtil.ts` | Core token parser — `$$internal$$` / `$$external$$` → HTML || `apps/host/src/components/utils/deepLinkHandlerUtil.tsx` | URL builder, validator, cookie read/write || `apps/host/src/components/utils/customDeepLinkMapper.ts` | Plugin handlers for custom module URL logic || `apps/host/src/components/utils/withDeepLink.tsx` | SSR HOC — JWT claim extraction, cookie fallback || `apps/host/src/pages/dl/index.tsx` | `/dl` route entry point || `apps/host/src/pages/mobiledl/index.tsx` | Native mobile app redirect || `apps/host/src/components/pages/Checkpoint/index.tsx` | Post-auth deep link execution or cookie handoff || `packages/journey/src/components/pages/JourneyApp/index.tsx` | Final `cpValue` cookie consumer after login completes || `packages/challenges/src/hooks/useChallengeDeepLink.ts` | Hook to generate challenge share URLs |---## Part 6 — Common Pitfalls- **`pageId` vs `pageid`** — The validator normalises `pageId` → `pageid` before parsing. The `urlMapper` keys always use lowercase `pageid`. Keep new templates consistent with lowercase.- **Cookie read-once semantics** — `dpLinkGetUtil` deletes the `cpValue` cookie immediately on read. Never call it twice expecting the same value.- **`{{DYNAMECONTEXT}}` placeholder** — The `internalDeepLinkHyperUrl` function emits this literal string for modal-only links. Scope:6. permanent fix for git lock issues8, Second instance of rulesapp in gcp There currently exist a manual process in the deployment of the kwatee application in GCPdue to the readwriteonce nature of the persistent volume claims(PVC)they cannot link to more than 1 pod at a timeand they are required for a pod to startup Harness deployment moves the new deployment folder to the GKE manifest and only deletes the old deployment folder once the new deployment folder is shown to be healthy and running.when Argo Syncs the manifest, due to seeing two deployment folders there will be two pods, one for the old deployment one for the new. The new one will be unable to start up, as the PVCs are unable to connect to the new pod as they remain linked to the old pod. As such the new pod will never start up, causing a deployment failure notice on harness, which will then proceed to delete tthe new deployment folder in the manifest in an attempt to rollback the failed deployment.Two potential approaches to solve this1) one approach is PVC attached to many pods (change readwriteonce to readwritemany This requires different storage structure and more restructuring than just a line change)2) second approach (this one also easy change in yaml) is to shut down old pod completely before we start new pod 2. set up github actions deployment for kwatee application and rulesui

*Notes*

https://github.com/cvs-health-source-code/RulesAppApplicationhttps://github.com/cvs-health-source-code/rulesApp_ui_v3.0.0 Explanation for Issue 3.ahm-rulesapp-application-svc.ahm-kwatee-dev.svc.cluster.local is the standard Kubernetes internal DNS format:                                                      <service-name>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local                                                                                                                                                                                           It is cluster-internal only and cannot be reached from outside the cluster because:                                                                                                                        1. The .cluster.local domain is resolved by CoreDNS (the cluster's internal DNS), not by any public or corporate DNS.                                                                   2. The DNS name is only resolvable from within pods running inside the same cluster.  3. There's no routing from outside the cluster to this address — external traffic must go through an Ingress, Istio Gateway, or a LoadBalancer/NodePort service.The .svc.cluster.local URL is only resolvable inside the cluster, so any attempt to access it from outside (a browser, Postman, external service, etc.) will fail. That's not an issue. The cron job pods run inside the cluster, so they can resolve it fine.

column6: [Vision] Ref Data: Implement process to load SCORE reference data into Redis cache
column7:
Implement new Java DAOs (Data Access Objects) to load data for the SCORE reference data tablesIncludes SCORE specific reference data, Clinical Reference data, and Supplier and Account specific reference data required by SCORE that is not already in RedisSee: https://github.com/cvs-health-source-code/Score/blob/master/clinicalanalyticssvr/src/main/java/net/ahm/careengine/clinicalanalyticssvr/cache/CARCacheManagerImpl.javahttps://github.com/cvs-health-source-code/Score/tree/master/clinicalanalyticssvr/src/main/java/net/ahm/careengine/clinicalanalyticssvr/refdata public static final String CAR_HEM_VALUES = ""CAR_HEM_VALUES"";public static final String CAR_SUCCESS_EXPRESSIONS = ""CAR_SUCCESS_EXPRESSIONS"";public static final String CAR_SEVERITY_LEVEL_SUCCESS_RATES = ""CAR_SEVERITY_LEVEL_AVG_SUCCESS_RATES""; // No longer usedpublic static final String CAR_ACTION_TYPE_DAY_RANGES = ""CAR_ACTION_TYPE_DAY_RANGES"";

----
*Notes*

The DAO (Data Access Object) layer is responsible for retrieving reference data from the PostgreSQL database using Spring's NamedParameterJdbcTemplate. Each DAO implementation extends BaseDAO (commit 6bb4f2e) and implements a domain-specific interface (e.g., MESuccessExpressionDAOIF). DAOs execute SQL queries to fetch records from database tables, map the result sets to Data Value Objects (DVOs), and organize them into structured collections—typically Map<String, List<T>> where the key is a composite business identifier. For example, MESuccessExpressionDAO (commit 090b722) queries the me_success_expression table, groups records by a composite key (monitored event ID + care component ID), and returns them in a map structure ready for caching. The Cache Loader (Repository) layer consumes the data from DAOs and persists it into Redis for fast in-memory access. Each repository implementation extends AbstractRedisRepository<T> (commit 090b722) and implements a domain-specific interface (e.g., MESuccessExpressionRepositoryIF). Repositories receive the pre-organized map from the DAO, serialize the DVO objects to JSON strings using org.json.JSONObject, and store them in Redis hash structures using Spring's RedisTemplate. For instance, MESuccessExpressionRepositoryImpl (commit 090b722) takes the map produced by the DAO and delegates to AbstractRedisRepository.innerAddToMap() to store each key-value pair in the Redis hash named by CacheNames.ME_SUCCESS_EXPRESSION, effectively building an in-memory cache that applications can query with sub-millisecond latency instead of hitting the database.

column6: CR - Molina NE Medicaid reg - Test Changes
column7:
Modified report requirements:
The enrollment date in the report should be the date the member was interactive and had completed a comprehensive nurse assessment (IRA, QTA, CM survey). The enrollment date may not necessarily be the date the member became interactive. The goal would be to not show members enrolled one month with their first completed assessment in the following month (s).If a member is interactive, then not interactive (closed eligibility, became self-directed, activity rule, refused, etc) the enrollment date would be the minimum date the member had a comprehensive nurse assessment following the members most recent accordant enrollment (the max date the member became interactive), unless a member was interactive, closed, then interactive within the same month. If that occurs the original enrollment date reported to the state would remainIf a member is under a different molina payer, state or LOB , then later flips payers to Molina NE Medicaid, the enrollment date and HRA date within the report should reflect when the member had their first assessment under their most recent NE Medicaid payer designation. The report should not reflect any dates or other information when the member was under a different payerIf a member flips to another LOB or state and no longer has the Molina NE Medicaid payer, the member should be reflected within the report with a closure date and closure reason. We will need requirements on what that closure date and closure reason should be. The DW does not have a payer tracking table of exact dates. So the closure date may need to the last day of the month the member switched payers (monthly snapshot).MRN's 2911350 and 2912103 need to be hard coded to be removed from all future 2026 reports since they have not been reported to the state. Someone on the business or clinical side will need to monitor these members to see if they should ever be included in a future report. Once members are hardcoded within a report they will no longer show up unless a requirement is receive to begin reporting them

Other potential requirements:
It is possible that all the EPIC data is not synched to the reporting data warehouse by the time the report needs to be generated and sent to the client (4th calendar day). It needs to be discussed internally how to handle within the requirements. So if a member becomes interactive and has their first completed assessment on the 30th of the month, however the EPIC assessment data is not captured in the DW by the 1st/2nd of the month, the member will not appear in that months report. However the following month they will appear with the historical dates of the prior month. How should this be handled in the report?It is recommended for reporting team to build and capture a stacked table to house data reported to Molina NE Medicaid regulatory . If the data historically reported to the client is captured in a stack table then DDAT can more easily update that historical data as requested then systematically generate the report again. We have similar tables for comp roster data, complaints data, quarterly data, etc. Having a stacked table could make manual updates easier, more accurate (remember we accidentally changed a HRA date by one day when doing a manual report change)

Modified report requirements:
The enrollment date in the report should be the date the member was interactive and had completed a comprehensive nurse assessment (IRA, QTA, CM survey). The enrollment date may not necessarily be the date the member became interactive. The goal would be to not show members enrolled one month with their first completed assessment in the following month (s).If a member is interactive, then not interactive (closed eligibility, became self-directed, activity rule, refused, etc) the enrollment date would be the minimum date the member had a comprehensive nurse assessment following the members most recent accordant enrollment (the max date the member became interactive), unless a member was interactive, closed, then interactive within the same month. If that occurs the original enrollment date reported to the state would remainIf a member is under a different molina payer, state or LOB , then later flips payers to Molina NE Medicaid, the enrollment date and HRA date within the report should reflect when the member had their first assessment under their most recent NE Medicaid payer designation. The report should not reflect any dates or other information when the member was under a different payerIf a member flips to another LOB or state and no longer has the Molina NE Medicaid payer, the member should be reflected within the report with a closure date and closure reason. We will need requirements on what that closure date and closure reason should be. The DW does not have a payer tracking table of exact dates. So the closure date may need to the last day of the month the member switched payers (monthly snapshot).MRN's 2911350 and 2912103 need to be hard coded to be removed from all future 2026 reports since they have not been reported to the state. Someone on the business or clinical side will need to monitor these members to see if they should ever be included in a future report. Once members are hardcoded within a report they will no longer show up unless a requirement is receive to begin reporting them

Other potential requirements:
It is possible that all the EPIC data is not synched to the reporting data warehouse by the time the report needs to be generated and sent to the client (4th calendar day). It needs to be discussed internally how to handle within the requirements. So if a member becomes interactive and has their first completed assessment on the 30th of the month, however the EPIC assessment data is not captured in the DW by the 1st/2nd of the month, the member will not appear in that months report. However the following month they will appear with the historical dates of the prior month. How should this be handled in the report?It is recommended for reporting team to build and capture a stacked table to house data reported to Molina NE Medicaid regulatory . If the data historically reported to the client is captured in a stack table then DDAT can more easily update that historical data as requested then systematically generate the report again. We have similar tables for comp roster data, complaints data, quarterly data, etc. Having a stacked table could make manual updates easier, more accurate (remember we accidentally changed a HRA date by one day when doing a manual report change)

Notes:
Approaches to create cost alerts: via Cloud Billing Budget API/ terraform script (To effectively track and alert on costs programmatically in GCP, the recommended best practice is to use the Cloud Billing Budget API rather than standard Cloud Monitoring (operational metrics for the Cloud Monitoring service itself)). Because billing metrics are tied to the GCP Billing Account, not the individual Project. Cloud Monitoring natively prioritizes showing your usage metrics for Google Cloud operations (Logging, Monitoring, Trace) within the project-level scoping. True billing cost metrics (such as estimated_charges) are strictly managed at the Billing Account level, not the individual Project level.via Google Budgets & Alerts which requires a proper roles to set. Decision is made to go with option 2 since it rovides best approach and less hurdles to achive the GCP resources budget cost alerts.
